title: Nest Patterns
content: ### **List of Contents** Switch Mode Nest Pattern Nest Option Nest Settings Reset Default Arrangement Snapshot #### **Efficiently layout patterns and check fabric consumption to use the least amount of fabric.** **** #### #### **Switch Mode** 1. Switch to Print Layout mode on the top-right corner of CLO. #### #### **Nest Patterns** **All Fabrics** 1. Click the ![Nest Patterns All On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45511429417369)**Nest Pattern** tool in the toolbar. → Patterns are efficiently placed on the fabric and the calculated value is displayed. 2. Click the **Stop Nesting** tool in the toolbar. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44216270067353)** **Current Fabric** Selectively re-nest a specific fabric while preserving the results of other fabrics. 1. Click and hold ![Nest Patterns All On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45511429417369)**Nest All Fabrics** tool to switch to ![Nest Patterns On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45511429419417) **Nest Current Fabric** tool. → Only the selected fabric in Print Layout Editor will be nested. All other fabrics will remain unchanged. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44216270067353)** **📝****Note:** * Directly click the pattern ▶ Drag it within the set fabric width to place it or place the pattern using [Align](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000306628-Align) and [Distribute](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000295167-Distribute). * Instead of waiting for nesting to complete, stop directly at any point in time to place patterns to save nesting time. * The number of calculations varies depending on the number of patterns. Higher counts give optimal arrangement results, but larger numbers of patterns require more calculations and take more time. Moving one space of the progress bar means that once the calculation has been completed. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44216270067353)** #### **Nest Option** CLO automatically identifies the visual characteristics of textures and prints, and optimizes Nesting to ensure continuity with maximum efficiency. 1. Set how the pattern is matched by right-clicking on it in Print Layout mode or under Fabric in the pattern properties in Simulation mode. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Texture Based** | CLO automatically detects the texture placement on each pattern and nests them with optimal efficiency by ensuring texture alignment. The same arrangement is consistently applied across all sizes based on how the patterns are stacked. **Print Based** | Similar to the above Texture-Based Matching, but with the added Print. **Lock in Place** | Locks the Base Size placement in Print Layout as is, while the remaining patterns follow the Texture-Based concept. **📝****Note:** When Pattern Matching is set, the texture movement is restricted when using Edit Texture tool to prevent misalignment. However, the restriction on texture movement can be unlocked using the Pattern Matching Lock option under Fabric in the pattern properties in Simulation mode if needed. #### #### **Nest Settings** 1. Click the **Nest Setting** tool in the toolbar. → Nesting Options appear in the Property Editor. 2. Set each property. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- **Nesting** | **Number of Garment** | Nest grading patterns on the fabric for mass production. By clicking the Select Grading button, manually set the size and quantity(amount) of the grading patterns to be nested. **📝****Note:****** Different colors can be displayed for each grading size on the fabric and you can check the size names. ([**![Youtube_Icon__1_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/29851942890777)**](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=Qig7DA2UUCJ6Wbpy&t=2301)[ Watch Video](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=Qig7DA2UUCJ6Wbpy&t=2301)) • Display grading colors: 2D Pattern Display » Show Grading Random Color icon • Display grading names: 2D Information Display » Show Grading Size icon **Group Each Sizes** | Click the **Group Each Sizes** option to nest patterns by grouping the graded sizes separately. (**![Youtube_Icon__1_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/29851942890777)**[ Watch Video](https://youtu.be/JcJVKJlNuNw)) **Colorway** | Nest patterns of all colorways on the fabric or click Select Colorway on the right to place only the selected colorway on the fabric. **Grain Direction** | **1-way** | Place the pattern in one orientation along the original grain direction **2-way** | Place the pattern in the opposite orientation that is 180 degrees from the original orientation to achieve optimized results. **4-way** | Place the pattern in four different orientations that are each 90 degrees from the original orientation to achieve optimized results. **One Bundle One Direction** | **OFF**(Default) | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55403002886809) Patterns within the same size/bundle can be placed in different orientations (randomly) to achieve maximum fabric efficiency. **ON** | All pattern pieces belonging to a single size (one bundle) will be restricted to the same orientation. While the nest as a whole uses 2-way or 4-way logic, each individual garment bundle maintains a consistent direction. **Buffer Spacing** | Set the spacing between patterns. **Pattern Dimension** | **Actual** | Place the pattern in its actual size. **Shrinkage** **/Growth** | Place the pattern with the shrinkage rate applied. **Information** | **Unit** | Set the units. **Fabric** | **Width** | Adjust the width of the fabric. **Length** | Check the total length of the fabric on which the pattern is placed. **Marker Length** | Set the length of the fabric manually to nest the pattern only up to the length of the set fabric. ([![Youtube_Icon__1_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/29851942890777) ](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=Qig7DA2UUCJ6Wbpy&t=2301)[Watch Video](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=Qig7DA2UUCJ6Wbpy&t=2301)) **Efficiency** | **Consumption** | Based on 100% of the total fabric, the fabric area consumed for the pattern is calculated as % **Remnant** | The remainder after subtracting the area consumed by the pattern is calculated as a %. **Area** | **Pattern Placed** | Check the pattern area placed on the fabric. **Remnant** | Check the remaining area where no pattern is placed. #### #### **Reset Default Arrangement** 1. Click the**Reset Default Arrangement** tool in the toolbar. → Patterns are reset to the initial arrangement state. #### #### **Snapshot** 1. Click the**Snapshot** tool in the toolbar. → 2D Snapshot pop-up window appears. 2. Set the size along with other options for the snapshot. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Size** | **Preset** | Select from a variety of presets. **Orientation** | Select the paper orientation. **Width** | Set the width of the image. **Height** | Set the height of the image. **Unit** | Set the unit of the print paper. **Resolution** | Set the resolution of the snapshot image. **Add'l Information** | Select the information that will appear in the Print Layout 2D snapshot. **Line Options** | Select the line that will appear in the Print Layout 2D snapshot. **Line Style** | Adjust the style of line in default Solid Line, Dotted Line, or Dashed Line. **Line Color** | Adjust the color of line. **Show Images** | Select the image that will appear in the Print Layout 2D snapshot. **Fabric Texture Opacity** | Adjust the opacity of the fabric and texture. **📝 Note:** Patterns and Internal Shapes with adhesion/bonding are classified separately in the **Bond** tab. #### Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: "Efficiently layout patterns and optimize fabric consumption for cost-effective garment production."

title: Express Cartoon
content: ### **New in 2026.0** **** This feature allows for a unique cartoon-style look using fabric and avatar materials. #### **Workflow** 1. Select a fabric style or an avatar. 2. In the Property Editor, set Material ▶ Type ▶**Toon (Viewport Only)**. 3. Adjust the displayed property values to achieve your desired style. #### #### **Options** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Base Color** | **Color** | Corresponds to MToon’s Lit Color parameter, representing the original color visible when receiving 100% light. **Base Color Map** | The texture map used for the Base Color **Opacity** | **Color** | Transparency settings for the Base Color. The overall transparency value. **Opacity Map** | Apply Common UI for assigning Texture Maps / Adding Maps. **Shade** | **Color** | The RGB color of the shadow. **Shade Color Map** | A texture applied specifically to shadow areas. Often uses the same texture as the Base Color or is left empty. **Hardness** | The degree of sharpness of the shadow edges. **Shift** | Adjusts the threshold where shadows begin to form. Higher values result in larger shadow areas. **Emission** | **Color** | Configures the parts that glow self-luminously, unaffected by external lighting. The color that glows brightly even in dark environments. **Emission Map** | The texture map used for parts that glow in the dark. **MatCap** | **Color** | MatCap is a fake refelction effect. The color to be blended with the MatCap image. **Matcap Map** | A texture that stores pre-captured ambient lighting information, layering a glossy effect on the surface based on the camera's viewing angle. **Rim Light** | **Color** | Rim Light(Halo) effect formed on the inner edges of the character. **Fresnel Power** | Adjusts the thickness and sharpness of the rim light. Controls the falloff of the light-affected area. **Lift** | Adjusts the position offset of the rim light. **Outline** | **Mode** | Creates a border line to achieve a cartoon-like aesthetic. Mode is the method of generating the outline. **Outline Map** | A texture used for masking to prevent outlines from appearing on specific areas. **Color** | The color of the line. **Width (mm)** | The thickness of the line. **📝****Note:** The Toon type is only visible in the Viewport and will not be applied to V-ray render.
content_description: Discover how to create a vibrant cartoon-style look for your avatars and fabrics with our new 2026.0 feature, complete with customizable materials and effects.

title: VRM Import/Export
content: ## **New in 2026.0** **** VRM file type is the most widely used 'universal format for 3D avatars' in the virtual metaverse. This is convenient 3D character file that allow you to import animation-style custom characters directly into the software without complex settings or conversion processes, enabling you to dress and fit garments while maintaining the character's unique appearance and movements. **📝 No****te:** The VRM file format is based on glTF 2.0, and the properties that can be controlled in the Import/Export VRM dialog box are identical to those of [**glTF 2.0**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360051525034-glTF-2-0-GLTF-GLB-File). #### **Import VRM** 1. Click **Main Menu** ▶ **File** ▶ **Import** ▶ **VRM** , specify the file path and name to display the Import VRM dialog. 2. Set the desired properties in the Import VRM dialog box, then click **OK** to load the file. #### #### **Export VRM** 1. Click **Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ VRM** , specify the destination path and file name to display the Export VRM dialog. 2. Set the properties in the Export VRM dialog box, then click **OK** to export the file. **📝****Note:** A VRM file can only be exported if it meets the following two conditions: * The top-level parent of the export target's joint root must form a single hierarchy. * It must have a humanoid skeleton structure.
content_description: Discover the new VRM file type in 2026.0, the universal format for 3D avatars that simplifies importing and exporting custom characters in the virtual metaverse, ensuring seamless integration of unique animations and styles.

title: NURBS Curve Support
content: ## **New in 2026.0** **** **NURBS (Non-Uniform Rational B-Splines)** curves created in external software can be displayed and converted into **3D Pen (Avatar)** for pattern generation. **📝****Note:** NURBS can only be used when loaded as an **Avatar type**. #### **Display NURBS** 1. Load a file containing **NURBS** data as an **Avatar type**. 2. Navigate to 3D Window ▶ Avatar DIsplay ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55527286897817) **Show Curve Lines** 를 활성합니다. 3. The NURBS curves are displayed. #### **Convert to 3D Pen (Avatar)** 1. Activate the**![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55527565320729) Select/Move **tool and select the NURBS. 2. Right-click to open the context menu and select **Convert to 3D Pen (Avatar)**. 3. As the NURBS and the 3D Pen (Avatar) overlap, deactivate **Show Curve Lines** to view the generated 3D Pen. 4. Use ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55527286899737) **Flatten** to generate a pattern from the closed area drawn with the 3D Pen.

title: Isolate Selection
content: **New in 2026.0** **** Display only selected elements in the 3D window. 1. Select the desired elements and click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55430497110809)**Isolate Selection** or press **Shift + I**. → Only the selected remain visible in the 3D window. 2. title: UV Editor
content: **List of Contents** **Open UV Editor** **Move UV** **Auto UV Packing** **UV Options** **Bake Textures** **UV Snapshot** **UV Display** **** Create UV maps of patterns, buttons, zippers and more to bake normal, roughness, metalness, and alpha maps. U is the horizontal axis and V is the vertical axis in the graph. ![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45595894327961) [Watch Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gt-YmEutZbk) #### **Open UV Editor** 1. Select Materials/UV ▶ **UV Editor** in the top menu. 2. Click the Map icon at the top-left corner of the UV Editor to switch to a different PBR map. #### **** #### **Move UV** 1. Click **Move UV** tool. 2. Set the moving distance. Distance 1 indicates the length of the segment of the UV Tile in the UV Editor. 3. Move the UV by clicking the arrow icon or pressing the directional keys on the keyboard. → UV is moved according to the distance you set. 4. Or click a pattern and drag to move its UVs. #### **** #### **Auto UV Packing** 1. Click**Auto UV Packing** tool. [![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/25701576108569) Watch Video](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=9IysllLmqtyUXtAV&t=4306) **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Option** | **Padding** | Sets the spacing between UVs. Values ​​are applied in a fraction of the UV tile size. (0.001 ~ 0.999) **Fidelity** | Adjust UV accuracy from 1 to 5. The higher the value, the more accurate the placement is as it is calculated in the original form, but as the amount of calculation increases, it takes more time. **Fix Scale Ratio** | Fix the size ratio of UVs. **Advanced Placement** | It is calculated in a more advanced way and is placed with optimal results with minimal empty space, but the larger the number of patterns, the more time it takes. **UV Area** | **0-1 (Default)** | Set to default 0-1 tile. **Selected Tile** | Set by directly entering UV coordinates. #### **UV Options** 1. Right-click on the desired pattern. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Select** | **All with Same Property** | All Patterns with the same particle distance, Layer and Fabric will be selected. **Select All Sewn** | Selects all patterns sewn to the initially selected pattern. 2. Or right-click on the background. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Arrange with UV** **(0-1)** | Fit All UV to 0-1. **Length (Absolute)** | Enter the actual distance value from the outline to offset the distance. **UV Coordinate (Relative)** | Enter a value between 0-1 from the outline to offset the distance. **Reset UV to 2D Arrangement** | Reset all UV to 2D Arrangements. #### #### **UV Bake Textures** 1. Click **Bake Textures** tool. 2. After setting the following options, click **Save**. **Options** | **Description** ---|--- **Saving Path** | Specify the saving path and the format (PNG / JPEG / PDF) for baked textures. **Size (Pixels)** | Set the size of the image. The image is saved as a square. **UV Area** | **0-1 (Default)** | Save the default 0-1 tile. **Selected Tile** | Save 1 selected tile. If users enter the UV coordinates to be saved, only one tile is saved. **All Tiles** | Save all tiles. **Fill Texture Seams** | The texture fills outside the seamline by the entered value in pixels. **Infinite Seams** | Fill the seamline to the entire area outside of the pattern. **Texture Type** | Select the type of texture to bake. #### **UV Snapshot** 1. Click **UV Snapshot** tool. 2. After setting the following options, click **Save**. **Options** | **Description** ---|--- **Saving Path** | Specifies the storage path for UV Snapshot. **Size (Pixels)** | Set the size of the image. The image is saved as a square and if the option "Anti-alias Lines" is checked, anti-aliasing is applied to the wire segment. **Edge Color** | Set the color of the wire segment. **UV Area** | **0-1 (Default)** | Save the default 0-1 tile. **Selected Tile** | Save 1 selected tile. If users enter the UV coordinates to be saved, only one tile is saved. **All Tiles** | Save all tiles. ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55501783845017) #### **UV Display** 1. Click the **UV Display** icon in the UV Editor. → Icons for UV display methods will appear. 2. Refer to the following to select the UV display target. **Options** | **Description** ---|--- **UV Display Target** | **Show All Objects** | Displays the UVs of all garments and avatars in the scene. **Show Selected Objects** | Displays only the UVs of the selected garments and avatars. **📝****Note:** The UV Display Element cannot be controlled when this option is activated. **UV Display Element** | **Show Garment** | Displays the UVs of garments. **Show Avatar** | Displays the UVs of avatars.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for creating, editing, and managing UV maps for textures in 3D modeling, including tools for baking textures, auto UV packing, and UV display options.

title: 3D File (FBX) Import/Export
content: **List of Contents** **Import FBX** **Export FBX** **** By Importing an FBX file, Geometry, Material, Joint, Camera, and Camera Animation information are also imported. **** #### **Import FBX** 1. Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import/Import (Add) ▶**FBX** → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click **OK**. → The Import FBX window appears. 3. Select the settings and click **OK**. → The FBX file is imported based on the setting. Basic | **Load Type** | Open or import the FBX file. ---|---|--- **Object Type** | Import the FBX file as Avatar or Trim. **Scale** | Select the unit or enter the specific value. **Object** | **Camera** | Toggles whether the Camera data or Camera Animation data is imported. **Animation** | Toggles whether the Animation data is imported. **Cache** **Animation (MC)** | Toggles whether the Cache Animation data is imported. **Axis Conversion** [**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142603909657)Watch Video**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=gL8VgdcciiEKfWLn&t=1538) | Change the direction of each axis of the object. **Option** | **Move Garment to Start Position** | Jump to the position of the start frame of the motion where the garment was loaded and move it.. **📝****Note:** Among the avatar skinning types, Dual Quaternion and Eblend are not compatible with CLO. **** #### **Export FBX** 1. Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶**FBX** → The Save File window appears. 2. Designate the file saving path and file name, and then click**OK**. → The Export OBJ window appears. 3. Select the settings as needed and click **OK**. → The file is exported as a FBX file based on the setting. **** **Object** **** **** **** **** **** **** **** | **Select an Avatar** | Select the avatar to be exported. The selected avatar is saved with its rigging data. You can exclude it as desired. ---|---|--- **Single/Multiple** | Exports selected objects as Single or Multiple Objects. ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360100786234) **Unweld/** **Weld** | When exporting, the connected Vertex(Mesh's points) where seamlines are set in the pattern are combined into individual objects or a single point. ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360102949453) **Weld selected Patterns in Workspace** | Weld the selected patterns connected by sewing lines. **Thin / Thick** | Sets whether to export geometry of the rendering thickness. **Unified UV Coordinates (PNG)** | Exports the texture information of all garment patterns to fit within the UV coordinate values between 0 and 1. Image Scale | Set image scales. Fill Texture Seams | This Function expands the range of the texture based on the border of the texture. **Include Internal Shapes** | The information of the Internal Line included in the garment is also exported. **Option** | **Animation** | When the FBX file is loaded, the animation information in the file is saved together. **Cache Animation (MC)** | Save the recorded garment animation as cache data together. **Basic** | **Scale** | Enter a number or select the desired unit from "Unit of file to be imported" and adjust the scale of the object. **Animation** | Entire Region | Save the recorded garment's animation entirely. Play Region | Only the garment animation in the play area is saved. **File Type** | Select whether to save as Binary / Ascii. * The file is stored in binary and cannot be opened by the user. * Ascii: The file is saved as text so the user can open and understand it. **Texture** | **Relative Texture Image File Path** | Save only the texture name without the texture image path, so if the saved FBX file and the texture image used in the file are in the same path, the texture image is automatically loaded. **Absolute Texture Image File Path** | Save the folder path where the texture image was located as the texture image path. If the path of the texture image is changed, the texture image cannot be loaded. **Embed Media (.zip)** | Export as a zip file along with the texture files used. **Diffuse Color Combined on Texture** | When a color is applied to the texture, it is saved as a combined color and texture. FBX files cannot contain all data, texture images and color values so select that option to export color information applied to textures as well. Animation | **Entire Region** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55505671959705) Exports the entire range where animation keys are set. **Play Region Only** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55505671959705) Exports only the animation within the specified playback range. **File** | **Save Colorways** | Export the garment with colorways Go back to the List of Contents

title: Animation Marker
content: ## **New in 2026.0** **** Animation Markers indicate significant points on the timeline or in space, allowing users to quickly identify the locations of scene transitions, events, and keyframes. Comments can be added to Markers to leave notes regarding editing intentions or task instructions. Additionally, they can be utilized as event triggers in the API via their names. #### **Add** 1. Open the **Animation Editor**. 2. Right-click the **Timeline Ruler** to display the context menu. 3. Click **Add** under the Marker group. 4. When the Marker dialog appears, set the name and frame of the Marker, then click OK. 5. Verify that a new Marker has been created at the specified frame. #### #### **Edit** 1. Hover the mouse over a created Marker to view its name and frame through the displayed tooltip. 2. To move a Marker, select and drag it to the left or right. 3. To edit a Marker's name, double-click the Marker or right-click it and select Edit from the context menu. 4. Modify the information in the displayed dialog, then click OK. 5. Verify that the changes have been applied to the Marker. #### #### **Copy and Paste** 1. Select one or more Markers. 2. Copy the Markers by pressing Ctrl+C or clicking Copy from the right-click context menu. 3. Specify the current frame using the playhead, then paste the Markers by pressing Ctrl+V or clicking Paste from the context menu. 4. The Markers will be pasted at the current frame indicated by the playhead. #### #### **Delete** 1. Select one or more Markers you wish to delete. 2. Press the Delete key or click Delete from the right-click context menu to remove the Markers.
content_description: Discover the powerful new Animation Markers in version 2026.0, designed to enhance your editing workflow by highlighting key points on the timeline, allowing for easy comments, event triggers, and efficient marker management.

content: #### Register an avatar accessory file or convert a pattern into an accessory. ![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44760225403161) [Watch Video](https://youtu.be/TApSQk7tXUY?si=MWBU0VR5tacpweKs) 1. title: Blend Shape Avatar
content: **New in 2026.0** **** Blend Shape is a technology that creates natural forms by blending various pre-made body types or facial expressions at desired ratios. With just a single base model, Blend Shape allows for real-time and flexible transformations, ranging from various target body sizes to subtle facial expressions. This feature enables users to import avatars containing Blend Shape data into CLO, allowing for instantaneous body changes and precise dynamic fitting. **📝****Note:** To use this feature, you should import files that contain Blend Shape data. #### **Blend Shape** 1. Load a file containing Blend Shape data as an Avatar type. 2. Go to Main Menu → Avatar → **Avatar Editor** to open the Avatar Editor 3. Click on the **Blend Shape** tab in the Avatar Editor 4. Check the list of **Deformable Parameters** included in the loaded avatar. 5. Adjust the weight of the desired part between 0 and 100 to modify the shape. #### #### **Set Options** **Select Avatar** * This option is displayed when multiple Blend Shape avatars are loaded; it will not appear if only a single avatar is present. * Selecting an avatar will display the corresponding Deformable Parameters for that specific avatar. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55480464118169)** **Deformable Parameters** * The list of deformable parameters included by the creator is grouped and displayed by mesh unit. * Each parameter can be set as a **Favorite**. By enabling **Show Favorites Only** in the top right, you can manage the list efficiently by displaying only your favorited items. * Clicking the **Reset** button will revert all unsaved changes to their initial values.

title: SHIMA SEIKI APEXFiz Plugin
content: ## **New in CLO 2026.0** **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/56360391337625)** **Recommended Specification** **Overview of How Data is Mapped** **Naming in APEXFiz and CLO** **Exporting Data from APEXFiz** **Importing Data to CLO** **Updating Design** **** _This plugin automates the connection of complex knit material data between_[ _APEXFiz_](https://www.shimaseiki.com/product/design/software/) _and CLO, including PBR textures, material layers, and part-based mapping._ #### **Recommended Specification** * **CLO:** 2026.0 or later versions * **APEXFiz:** V-09C or later versions #### **Overview of How Data is Mapped** * **Part-to-Pattern Mapping:** Each **Part created in APEXFiz** is mapped to a **Pattern piece in CLO**. * **Exact Name Matching:** The mapping is triggered by an exact match of the 'Part Name'. * **Automated Material Assignment:** Once a match is found, the plugin applies all associated materials and PBR textures specifically to that matched part. #### **Naming in APEXFiz and CLO** 1. Once the knit design is finalized in **APEXFiz** , check each **Part Name**. 2. In **CLO** , the **Pattern Name** must match **APEXFiz's Part Name** exactly. _**📝 Note:**_ \- _Using single-byte alphanumeric characters (A-Z, 0-9) for naming._ \- _Avoid using double-byte characters (e.g., Kanji, Cyrillic) or special characters \ / : * ? " < > | for naming._ #### **Exporting Data from APEXFiz** 1. In **APEXFiz,** navigate to the **3D Mapping Editor** ▶ Click the **"▼" (arrow)** next to the **Save icon** ▶ Select **Export to CLO**. → Show a pop-up menu of Export to CLO. 2. Set the Colorway, Resolution, Name, and File Type for export. 3. Click **Default** to set the default export path. _Default Path: C:\Users\Public\Documents\CLO\External\ShimaSeiki\APEXFiz\_ _**📝 Note:** Default Path is required for automatically recognizing files and ensuring smoother data transactions. _ 4. Click **Execute.** → A main folder is created, containing individual sub-folders for each part. Folders follow the naming in '**Name_Colorway_PartName** '. → Each sub-folder contains U3M material data and PBR texture maps. ![1_ExportingDatafromAPEXFiz_gif.gif](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/56836676591129) #### **Importing Data to CLO** 1. In **CLO** , open a**** project file****(**ZPRJ**), garment file (**ZPAC**), or patterns (**DXF**). 2. Check if the**Pattern Name** in **CLO** matches the **Part Name** in **APEXFiz**. 3. Navigate to **Main Menu** ▶ **Plugins** ▶ **APEXFiz** ▶ Select **Import from APEXFiz**. → Load PBR textures → Map materials to each pattern automatically based on name matching. _**✨Tip:** _ _\- Use![Edit-Texture.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/56360623941657) _[_**Edit Texture**_](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002680348-Edit-Texture) _to scale or reposition textures directly on the patterns or the 3D garment._ _\- Access_[ _**Print Layout Mode**_](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013408108-Edit-Fabric-Print-Layout-Mode) _to align patterns precisely against the texture map._ ![2_ImportingDatatoCLO_gif.gif](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/56836695302425) #### **Updating Design** 1. In **APEXFiz** , modify the design. 2. Re-export by following Exporting Data from APEXFiz. 3. Re-import to CLO by following Importing Data to CLO.

title: Set Fabric Materials
content: #### **List of Contents** Fabric Properties Material Type Base Color Normal Map Displacement Map Opacity Reflection #### **Express texture or pattern of the fabric.![Youtube Icon \(1\).png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55527645292185) **[**Watch Video**](https://youtu.be/IuClc5u5wcg) #### **Fabric Properties** 1. Click a fabric in ![Fabric Tab.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38101235323545) **Fabric** tab in [Object Browser](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000374247-%EB%AC%BC%EC%B2%B4%EC%B0%BD-Object-Browser-). 2. Set the material properties in Property Editor. 3. Select the Front, Back, or Side tab to set the material properties for each side of the fabric. **📝****Note:** In the Back or Side tab, turn off Use Same Material as Front to apply different materials, or enable Use Same Color as Front to match the back and side color with the front. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38107403704601)** ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55473976669081) After clicking the Back tab and turning off Use Same Material as Front, the Swap Front & Back button appears, allowing you to swap the front and back material properties. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55473976673049) #### #### **Material Type** 1. Set the appropriate [CLO Material Type](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115015998728-Material-Type). #### #### **Base Color** **Color** 1. Set the [color](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360047316974-Fabric-Color) of the fabric. **Base Color Map** 1. Click the **Open** button to apply the Base Color Map. **📝****Note:** Through the option of [User Setting](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002563607-Set-Default-Files), you can convert the color profile of the image to sRGB when loading textures. 2. Set the Recolor option as needed. **• Desaturate** Desaturate the entire Base Color Map to remove color and convert it into grayscale or black and white. **• Color Switch** ![Youtube Icon \(1\).png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55527645292185) [Watch Video](https://youtu.be/8sfPSGnNpG4) Easily and quickly switch the color of solid fabric to a new one without losing the accuracy of the chosen color. ![Switch Color.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38116673801369) ******📝****Note:** It is recommended to use the [Texture Editor](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360053351314-Texture-Editor#Click4) if the Base Color Map contains multiple colors, as it may not be switched properly. Please note that this Switch option is not synced with the Switch option in the Texture Editor. #### **Normal Map** Express uneven texture more realistically. 1. When a texture is applied, Normal Map is generated by adjusting the Intensity. 2. Or click the **Open** button to manually apply Normal Map image. #### #### **Displacement Map** Express thickness or bumpiness of fabrics or textures. You can find more detailed information [here](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360025439933-Displacement-Map-ver5-1-0). #### #### **Opacity** **Opacity** 1. Adjust the Opacity value to apply transparency to the fabric overall. **Opacity Map** Adjust level of transparency using a grayscale image map. 1. Set the mode to determine whether the map's alpha value is encoded in the RGB channel or the alpha channel. 2. Click the **Open** button to apply Opacity Map. #### #### **Reflection** **Roughness** 1. Set whether to adjust the Roughness with the intensity value or apply it as a specific map. 2. Adjust the values to express fabric gloss. 3. Check the Invert option to make the shiny parts becomes dull and vice versa when using the map. **Reflection** 1. Adjust the intensity value to express fabric reflection. **Metalness** 1. Adjust the value to apply metallics to the fabric overall. 2. Or click the **Open** button to partially apply metallics using a grayscale image. * The white parts of the map appear metallic. **📝****Note:** • When working with **Metalness Map** , control **Roughness Intensity** and **Reflection Intensity** level that are suitable for the metallic texture. (e.g. Roughness Intensity 10, Reflection Intensity 90) • For the non-metallic areas (matte), assign the same metalness map to **Roughness Map,** and turn on **Invert**. #### Go back to the List of Contents

content: Create OBJ Register OBJ **** Register your own OBJ file as a Slider/Puller/Stopper. **** **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Zipper ▶ Register OBJ Property Editor ▶ Shape ▶ ![plus_button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/25189692962201) #### **Create OBJ** Check the requirements below when making OBJs in other 3D programs. **※ Essential** * Set the name of the MESH to **Slider and Puller** when creating an OBJ with a slider and a puller. ![Slider_Puller_name.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900006815406) * For each type, adjust the position to suit the meaning of the axis. (If the position of the axis is not correct, the OBJ may not be loaded in the correct position) **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Slider** | **X-Axis** | Position the shoulder of the slider where zipper teeth insert on the X-axis 0. **Y-Axis** | The direction the slider moves is the Y-axis, Position center of the slider where the center of the zipper teeth aligned at 0 of the Y-axis. **Z-Axis** | Position the Z-axis 0 where the side of the zipper teeth is located. ![Slider.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900006815306) **Sto** pper | The stopper configured on both sides must be made to be the same scale as the two OBJ axes. **X-Axis** | Position the shoulder of the slider where zipper teeth insert on the X-axis 0. **Y-Axis** | **Top Stopper** Position the point where the most end (top) of the zipper blade is in contact with the Y-axis 0. **Bottom Stopper** When the slider is lowered all the way, the point where it touches the bottom of the slider is positioned on the Y-axis at 0. **Z-Axis** | Position the Z-axis 0 where the side of the zipper teeth is located. ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900007735143) ![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900007735083) ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900006815506) **Puller** | Place the position where the slider is attached at the origin (0,0,0). _**✨Tip:**_ The puller position is adjustable within the CLO. ![Puller.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900006815366) **Slider & Puller** | Create sliders & pullers are created based on the slider axis. ![Slider_Puller.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900007734823) **** #### **Register OBJ** 1. Click the Materials ▶ Zipper ▶**Register OBJ** in the top menus. After setting the following options, click the**OK** button. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Basic** | **Type** | Select the type (Slider, Puller, Stopper, Slider & Puller) to register the OBJ. **Name** | Enter a file name. **Scale** | Adjust the size of the OBJ. **Axis Conversion** | Change each axis of the OBJ. **File** | **OBJ** | Slider / Puller | Load the OBJ file you want to register. Stopper (Top, Bottom-Open) | Load each Top and Botton-Open OBJ file. The first OBJ loaded is placed in the direction of the zipper created first. Slider & Puller | Load a combined zipper OBJ file. Select and assign the mesh item of Slider and Puller in the Select Mesh menu. Teeth | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55639131982745) Load the OBJ file to register as the zipper teeth. The spacing between the teeth is set to 0 mm by default. Adjust the spacing while previewing the result in the preview window. **Preview** | Check the imported OBJ file in advance. **Puller Position** | For Slider or Slider & Puller type. title: Tape Measure
content: ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55718294111129) **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55718301943193)** #### ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55718294114457)**Tape Measure (Point-to-Point)** #### **Objective** Measure the precise distance between two points on the fabric layout to verify alignment, pattern matching, or spacing between nested pattern pieces. **Location** Print Layout Editor ▶ Vertical Toolbar ▶ **Tape Measure (Point-to-Point)** * * * ### **Operation** 1. **Select Tool** : Click the **Tape Measure (Point-to-Point)** icon from the vertical toolbar. 2. **Define Start Point** : Click on a point, edge, or specific location on a pattern piece to establish the beginning of the measurement. 3. **Define End Point** : Click on a second point (either on the same pattern piece or a different one) to finish the measurement. * A dashed green line will appear, displaying the distance between the two points in the current unit of measure. 4. **New Measurement** : Click again to start a new measurement. **📝********Note:** Only one active measurement is displayed at a time; creating a new start point will clear the previous measurement.

title: Trace
content: **List of Contents** Trace as a Pattern Trace as an Internal Shape Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes Trace as Point of Measure(POM) **** Use the Trace function to convert lines/shapes/area/[guidelines ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360010960074)to Patterns. #### **Trace as a Pattern** 1. Select the ![Trace.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53165337024409) **Trace** tool in the 2D toolbar. 2. Select the Baselines, Internal Lines, or Outlines to be traced. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55475233738265)** ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55473680021017) Select the Baselines, Internal Lines, or Outlines on both sides of the half-symmetry pattern. → The half-symmetry relationship on the newly traced pattern can be maintained. Internal lines and Baselines within the selection range are contained in the traced pattern. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55473724912153) **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55475233738265)** 3. Right-click on the selected Baselines, Internal Lines, or Outlines to access the pop-up menu. 4. Select **Trace as a Pattern**. →The selected Baselines, Internal Lines, or Outlines are traced as a Pattern. #### **Trace as an Internal Shape** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location 2. Select the Baselines to be traced. 3. Right-click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. 4. Select **Trace as an Internal Shape**. →When the selected lines are intersected, the intersection is joined and the lines are traced as one shape. #### **Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location 2. Select the Baselines to be traced. 3. Right-click on the selected Baselines to access the pop-up menu. 4. Select **Trace as Internal Lines/Shapes**. →The selected lines are traced as they are. #### **Trace as**[**POM**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360025716774-2D-%EC%A4%84%EC%9E%90-%EC%83%9D%EC%84%B1) 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location 2. Select the Baselines, Internal Lines or Outlines to be traced. 3. Right-click on the selected lines to access the pop-up menu. 4. Select **Trace as Point of Measure** → The selected line is traced as POM. → When more than two segments of different patterns are clicked, they are traced as a group POM. At this time, the connected points are randomly designated. **📝****Note:** * To easily select a closed shape, double-click on the Internal Line. * Click and drag to select multiple Internal Lines at once. All Internal Lines within the marquee box are selected. * Occasionally, Internal Lines may not be connected precisely when dxf files are imported into CLO from other 2D CAD programs. If the selected lines are less than 0.5mm apart, they are traced as a closed shape as they are recognized as adjacent lines. However, on the other hand, if the selected lines are more than 0.5mm apart, they are traced as individual Internal Lines as they are recognized as separate lines. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Explore the various tracing functions in CLO 3D to convert lines, shapes, and areas into patterns, internal shapes, and points of measure for enhanced design accuracy and efficiency.

content: #### **List of Contents** Create Edit Link Annotation to Line Show/Hide #### Set the orientation, size, and color of pattern annotations for quick and clear access to pattern information. #### #### **Create** 1. Click 2D toolbar ▶ ![Pattern Annotation On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44512372632217) **Pattern Annotation** tool. 2. Click the Pattern to add an annotation, then press **Ctrl + Enter** on the keyboard or click anywhere else to complete. #### #### **Edit** 1. Click 2D toolbar ▶ ![Edit Annotation On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44512372633625)**Edit Annotation** tool. 2. Move the added annotation by clicking and dragging, or rotate it by clicking and dragging the pivot point in the desired direction. 3. Click the annotation, then set the properties in the Property Editor. **Property** | **Description** ---|--- **Orientation** | Set the orientation of the annotation. **Font Size** | Adjust the font size of the annotation. **Color** | Change the color of the annotation. 4. Right-click the annotation to set options as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Delete** | Delete the selected annotation. **Copy & Paste** | Copy the annotation and paste it at the desired position **Rotate** | Rotate the annotation in the desired direction. #### ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55407387496985) #### **Link Annotation to Line/Point** Link Pattern Annotations to specific Pattern Outlines/points or Internal Lines/points to maintain their relative position when patterns are modified. 1. Select the **Edit Annotation** tool from the 2D toolbar. 2. Right-click on the annotation in the 2D window, and select **Link to**. 3. title: Custom Measurements
content: **New in 2026.0** **Add Custom Measurements** **Adjust Placement** **** Precisely measure and set the placement of a graphic by measuring from specific anchor points on the graphic to the Pattern Outline. #### **Add Custom Measurements** **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55409872795545)** **Straight line Custom Measurements** 1. Select the **Transform Graphic** tool from the 2D toolbar. 2. **Right-click** the graphic in the 2D window and select **Custom Measurements.** 3. Click the Pattern Outline directly within the horizontal or vertical range of the graphic to automatically create a straight-line measurement. **Lock to** | **Graphic Outline** (default) | Tethers the measurement anchor primarily to the **Graphic Outline**. The measurement anchor point follows the graphic's transformations; if the graphic is scaled or moved, the measurement persists relative to the artwork's edges. ---|---|--- **Pattern Outline** | Tethers the measurement anchor primarily to the **Pattern Outline**. The anchor point remains fixed on the pattern; moving the graphic manually will update the measurement distance while the pattern anchor stays in its original static position. #### **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55409872795545)** **X &Y Measurement Coordinates** 1. Select the **Transform Graphic** tool from the 2D toolbar. 2. **Right-click** the graphic in the 2D window and select **Custom Measurements**. 3. Select the starting point **on the graphic** : * **Free Selection** : Click anywhere within the graphic area. * **Snap Selection** : Hold the **Shift** key to display the graphic’s bounding box corners, center, and midpoints. The system also provides point recommendations based on the graphic image itself. * The cursor will automatically snap to the nearest recommended point for easier selection. 4. Move the cursor and click on the target **Pattern Outline/Point** to establish the measurement. #### #### **Adjusting Placement** 1. Once the measurement is established, use the **Placement** Input Box in the Property Editor for exact coordinate control: **X & Y** | Enter specific values to define the distance between the pattern outline (or point) and the anchor point on the graphic. ---|--- **Graphic Movement** | Confirming these values moves the entire graphic to the precise coordinates relative to the pattern. **Instant Sync** | The graphic position updates immediately in both 2D and 3D windows. **📝 Note:** * **Smart Snapping** When holding **Shift** , the recommended points are dynamically generated based on the graphic’s visual style and geometry, allowing for more intuitive placement relative to the artwork's design. _**✨**_**Tips:** * **Direct Calculation** Instead of calculating the final distance manually, you can type basic equations (e.g., `50 + 15` or `100 / 2`) into the X or Y input fields. * **Relative Adjustments** This allows you to shift the graphic by a specific increment relative to its current measured distance without clearing the existing value. * **Efficiency** The software will automatically solve the equation and move the entire graphic to the resulting coordinate immediately.
content_description: Discover the powerful new features in version 2026.0 that allow you to add custom measurements and precisely adjust the placement of graphics with intuitive control and instant syncing across your design workspace.

title: Gluing
content: **New in 2026.0** **Glue Fill** **Glue Brush** **Sticker** Bond two pattern pieces together by adding glue to the entire pattern or a designated area. This feature allows secondary pieces like pockets, labels, or reinforcements to follow the movement and deformation of a base pattern during simulation. The Glue tools provide multiple methods for securing overlapping patterns, ranging from automatic boundary detection to free-hand painting and ghost-shape placement. **** #### **Glue Fill** Automatically detects the boundaries of a pattern or an internal shape to apply glue. Placing the secondary pattern in the 2D or 3D window defines the glue area between the patterns. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **In the 2D Window** 1. Position the secondary pattern (the piece to be glued) directly **on top** of the base pattern. 2. Ensure the patterns overlap exactly where you want the bond to be established. 3. Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331100441)Glue Fill** tool and click on the secondary pattern or the secondary pattern’s internal shape(if any). → The overlap establishes the bonding relationship between the two layers. 4. Move the secondary outside the base pattern (optional). **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **In the 3D Window** 1. If the patterns are not draped, position the secondary pattern over the base pattern. 2. If the garment is draped, then the secondary pattern must be **draped over or under** the base pattern (in contact or close proximity). 3. Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331100441)Glue Fill** tool and click on the secondary pattern. → The glue will be applied to the respective contact area between the layers. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **Set Options** 1. Set the mode if needed. **Add** | Applies glue to the whole pattern shape or its internal shape. ---|--- **Subtract** | Completely removes glue from the pattern. #### **Glue Brush** Allows for free-hand drawing of glue onto the pattern. The tool requires a layered relationship between two patterns to function. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **In the 2D Window** 1. Position the secondary pattern (the piece to be glued) directly **on top** of the base pattern. 2. Ensure the patterns overlap in the area where you want the glue to be applied. 3. Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331100569)****Glue Brush** tool and click and drag on the pattern to paint the glue area, which appears as an orange highlight. 4. Once the desired area is painted, the secondary pattern will follow the movement and deformation of the painted area on the base fabric during simulation. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **In the 3D Window** 1. If the patterns are not draped, position the secondary pattern over the base pattern. 2. If the garment is draped, then the secondary pattern must be **draped over or under** the base pattern (in contact or close proximity). 3. Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331100569)****Glue Brush** tool and click and drag on the pattern to paint the glue area, which appears as an orange highlight. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55248331099929)** **Set Options** 1. Set the options if needed. **Type** | **Over** | Applies glue to the underside of the secondary pattern piece to bond with the pattern beneath it. ---|---|--- **Under** | Applies glue to the top surface of the base pattern piece to bond with the pattern above it. **Mode** | **Add** | Paint new adhesive areas onto the pattern surfaces. **Subtract** | Use this mode to partially remove existing glue by painting over the previously highlighted orange areas. **Size** | Allows you to adjust the width of the glue stroke for more precise or broader application. **** #### **Sticker** Mimics a real-world sticking process by allowing you to "pick up" a pattern piece and use a ghost pattern shape to precisely target and apply it to a specific area. 1. Select the **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55307548131481)****Sticker** tool in the 2D window. 2. Click on the desired secondary pattern piece (e.g., a pocket or label) to select it. 3. A **ghost pattern shape** (transparent preview) will appear and follow your cursor. 4. Move the ghost shape over the base pattern to target the desired placement area. 5. Click at the specific location on the base pattern to "stick" the piece in place. 6. View the results immediately in the 3D window as the pattern conforms to the target area. ****
content_description: Discover the innovative **Glue Fill**, **Glue Brush**, and **Sticker** tools in 2026.0, designed to seamlessly bond, customize, and position pattern pieces for enhanced simulation and design flexibility.

title: Lacing
content: **New in 2026.0** **Define Path** **Set Options** **** Automate the lacing process by guiding the lacing pattern and direction through designated holes. This tool eliminates manual intervention by automatically routing the cord and generating an editable pattern for further customization. **** #### **Define Path** 1. Select the **![Lacing On.svg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55445403327257)****Lacing Tool** from the 2D Toolbar. 2. Click the **starting hole** where the lacing begins or where the cord is first inserted. 3. Click the **next hole** in your desired sequence. 4. Continue clicking holes until you reach the **last** or **exit hole.** **** 5. To complete the sequence, **double-click** the final hole or press **Enter**. 6. An **editable lace pattern** will automatically generate in the 2D window for further modifications. **** #### **Set Options** After finalizing the path, you can reverse its direction or adjust its curvature. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55479973887385)** **Reverse Direction** 1. Immediately after finalizing the path, a **reverse icon** ![Reverse.svg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55445403327769)will appear attached to your cursor. 2. Click a specific hole to **reverse the lacing direction** at that point. E.g., changing if the cord enters from the top or bottom of the eyelet. 3. Check the 3D window to see the routing changes update in real-time. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55479973887385)** **Adjust Curvature** ![image.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55445420203033) 1. Adjust the cord's arc using the slider. Increasing curvature helps stabilize simulation by preventing the cord from colliding with or clipping into nearby patterns. **** **📝 Note:** The generated lace is a standard pattern piece; you can independently edit its thickness, material, or physical properties in the Property Editor like any other garment part. **✨ Tip:** If the cord enters an eyelet from the wrong side in 3D, use the **reverse icon** to flip the orientation without redrawing the entire path.
content_description: Discover the new **Define Path** tool in 2026.0 that automates and customizes lacing patterns, allowing for easy adjustments in direction and curvature for seamless design integration.

title: [Fit Map] Strain Map
content: **** Check how much the garment or fabric stretches under external stress as a percentage. **** 1. Click and hold the ![Fit Maps Off Hover.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/56769397284889) **Fit Map** icon, and select ![Fit Maps Strain Map Hover.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/56769382270745) **Strain Map**(Alt + 7). → Shows how much the garment is stretched as a percentage. 2. Adjust the settings in the Strain Map window. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Global** | Global Mode uses the same scale in the Strain Map, making it easy to see how much a pattern has stretched from its original shape, regardless of fabric type. **Range** | The Strain Map divides the range from the base 100% (no strain) to your defined maximum into 8 segments. **Blue:** Indicates 100% stretch, meaning no strain or deformation. **Red:** Indicates the defined maximum (e.g., 120%), representing the upper limit of stretch. **Gradation:** Values between 100% and the maximum are linearly calculated and expressed as a smooth color gradient. **📝****Note:** You can manually adjust the colors by clicking the each color chip. **Fabric** | Fabric Mode uses each fabric’s stretch limit in the Strain Map, making it easier to see a more accurate and realistic fit. **Range** | The Strain Map divides the range from 100% (no strain) to the fabric’s maximum stretch into 8 segments. **📝****Note:** Each color chip can be selected to manually adjust the colors. **Stretch** | The wearable stretch limit is automatically calculated and applied based on each fabric's physical properties. The stretch limit is the point where the fabric can no longer stretch comfortably under a standard level of force, meaning the garment becomes too uncomfortable to wear. For example, stiff fabrics reach this limit with minimal stretch, while flexible fabrics can stretch much more before reaching their capacity. **📝****Note:** You can manually adjust the maximum stretch as needed. 3. Click a point on the simulated 3D garment to see detailed values at that location. **Dominant Direction** Indicates the specific direction (Warp, Weft, or Bias) that is closest to its stretch limit. **Actual Strectch** Shows the raw physical stretch percentage in the Dominant Direction. **Force** Calculates how close the fabric is to its maximum stretch capacity, where 100% represents the fabric's defined limit. Exceeding 100% means the fabric has been stretched beyond its defined capacity.
content_description: Discover how to assess the stretch capacity of garments and fabrics under external stress using our interactive Strain Map tool, which visually represents stretch percentages and helps ensure optimal fit and comfort.

title: 3D Pencil (Avatar)
content: **New in 2026.0** Sketch Set Options Convert to 3D Pen **** Sketch directly on the avatar and turn your lines into patterns instantly. #### **Sketch** 1. [Open an avatar](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002687268-Avatar-AVT-Open-Add-Save#h_01KJBWPJ36BCHSD19S856T5RK5) in the 3D window to being sketching. 2. In the 3D toolbar, press and hold the **![3D Pen Avatar On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55500528789785)3D Pen (Avatar)** and switch to the ![3D Pencil Avatar On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55500553607449) **3D Pencil (Avatar)**. → The Sketch window appears, and the viewpoint switches to the front view. **📝****Note:** To ensure proper conversion to 3D Pen after sketching, the 3D view is fixed to either the front or back view. Only zooming is available. 3. Click and drag on the avatar to sketch your design. 4. Change the type to **![Eraser.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55500528790937)Eraser** , then click and drag over the area you want to remove. → The lines within the dragged area are removed. #### **Set Options** 1. Set the following options as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Type** | **Pencil** | **Symmetry** | Applies symmetrical sketching based on the avatar’s center axis. **Conversion** **Guide** | Before converting to 3D Pen, you can see how your sketch will be converted. The segment points shown on the guide line are important, as areas without points will turn into curves. If you need a corner or a defined angle, make sure a point is present at that position. If a corner is missing a point, the edge may become rounded unintentionally. We recommend reviewing the guide and adjusting your lines to achieve the best results before converting. **Eraser** | **Size** | Adjust the eraser size to control how much is removed at once. **Viewpoint** | Switch the 3D viewpoint to either the front or back. #### **Convert to 3D Pen** 1. Click the **Convert to 3D Pen** in the Sketch window. → The lines drawn on the avatar are converted to 3D Pen, and the tool automatically switches to the ![Edit 3D Pen Avatar On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55500528791961)**Edit 3D Pen (Avatar).** 2. Check the converted 3D Pen and [edit ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115008890367-Edit-3D-Pen-Avatar)it directly as needed. _**✨Tip:** For 3D Pens created by sketching on both the front and back simultaneously,_[_flattening_](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115008890627-Flatten) _both sides automatically sews the front and back together._
content_description: Explore the new 2026.0 features that allow you to sketch directly on avatars and seamlessly convert your designs into 3D Pen patterns for enhanced creativity in fashion design.

title: CLO system requirements (March 2026)
content: This document describes the specifications and precautions that your computer must meet to install, launch, and operate the CLO software. **Windows** Category | **Minimum** | **Recommended** ---|---|--- OS | Windows 11 64-bit (24H2) 1) | Windows 11 64-bit (25H2) Processor | AMD® Ryzen™ 3000 series Intel® 8th-Gen series 2) | AMD® Ryzen™ 9000 series or higher Intel® i9 14th-Gen or higher Memory | 16GB | 64GB 3) Graphics card | AMD, Intel, Nvidia GPUs supporting OpenGL 1.6 or higher | NVIDIA® GeForce RTX 4000 series or NVIDIA® RTX A, RTX Ada, RTX Pro Blackwell series 4) 5) 6) 7) Storage | SSD 10GB or more | SSD 20GB or more Screen | 1920x1080 (FHD) | 2560x1440 (QHD), 3840x2160 (UHD, 4K) Input device | 3-button mouse | 3-button mouse Network | Internet connection required | Internet connection required 1)****[**Windows 10 support has ended on October 14, 2025**](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/windows-10-support-has-ended-on-october-14-2025-2ca8b313-1946-43d3-b55c-2b95b107f281). Strongly recommend using Windows 11. 2) A processor that supports [**AVX2**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advanced_Vector_Extensions) is required to use the VRay render function built into CLO software. As a simple example, Intel 3rd generation and earlier processors cannot use CLO's VRay render. 3) To use the basic functions of CLO software, 16GB of memory is required; for smoother operation, 32GB of memory is needed; and for very heavy and complex clothing, animations, and ultra-high-quality rendering, 64GB or more of memory is required. 4) CLO utilizes [**Nvidia CUDA**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CUDA) acceleration technology for CLO GPU-Simulation and Rendering. So computers with only Intel Graphics or AMD graphics card do not benefit from GPU acceleration that speeds up CLO simulation and rendering. If you want faster GPU-simulation and GPU-rendering in CLO software, look for a computer with a recent Nvidia graphics card. 5) For graphics card related issues, please see the following guide. In particular, please update your graphics card driver to the latest. [**Graphics Card Problems and Troubleshooting**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000296768) 6) A GPU that supports OpenGL Compatibility Profile 1.6 or higher is required to run CLO software. Some mobile GPU processors from AMD and Intel may not fully support [**OpenGL**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenGL), which is essential for running CLO software, and may not run CLO software. If you are using a laptop or graphics card with a built-in CPU, check with the hardware manufacturer for the GPU model and whether it supports OpenGL. 7) Recommend a graphics card with at least 4GB of dedicated video memory (GPU memory, VRAM). For high-quality VRay rendering and heavy GPU simulations, 12GB or more of dedicated video memory is required. * * * **macOS** Category | **Minimum** | **Recommended** ---|---|--- Mac models | Apple Silicon Mac: M1 1) | Apple Silicon Macs: M1, M2, M3, M4 macOS | Sonoma 14 *For macOS dependencies, check out the notes below 2) | Sequoia 15, Tahoe 26 Processor | Apple Silicon Chip | Apple Silicon Chip 3) Memory | 16GB | 64GB 4) Storage | SSD 10GB or more | SSD 20GB or more Screen | 1920x1080 (FHD) | Retina 4K, Retina 5K supported Input devices | 3-button mouse | 3-button mouse Network | Internet connection required | Internet connection required 1) [**Apple announced that Apple is ending support for Intel-powered Macs with macOS Tahoe**](https://www.wired.com/story/macos-tahoe-last-update-for-intel-macs/). 2) Starting with CLO v2024, the minimum macOS has been changed to Monterey 12. See which macs are compatible with macOS Monterey 12 here. [**macOS Monterey is compatible with these computers**.](https://support.apple.com/en-us/103260) 3) Starting with CLO version 2025.0, V-Ray rendering via GPU acceleration is available on Apple Silicon Macs. It is GPU (Metal) that can be selected from the Render Engine list, and the GPU simulation on Apple Silicon Mac is under research and development. [**See how to Edit-VRay-Render-Properties**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014899148-Edit-V-Ray-Render-Properties). 4) To use the basic functions of CLO software, 16GB of memory is required; for smoother operation, 32GB of memory is needed; and for very heavy and complex clothing, animations, and ultra-high-quality rendering, 64GB or more of memory is required. * * * **Please note** * CLO software does not support garment pattern digitizers. * CLO software have tested and supports Wacom® tablet products, and compatibility issues may occur with third-party tablets. * CLO software does not support BootCamp in macOS, also does not support similar desktop virtualization apps. * CLO software does not support 32-bit OS (e.g. Windows 7 32-bit), Apple iOS, iPad OS, tvOS, Android OS, ChromeOS, Windows Mobile and Linux. * CLO software can be downloaded as .exe or .dmg file format via [**CLO official website**](https://clo3d.com/en/clo/download/installer). It is not distributed in .msi or .pkg file format. * CLO software can be installed and run in virtual server environments such as Virtual Machine and Virtual Desktop Infrastructure and in cloud services. However, in this case, the CLO team does not provide technical support. **See also** * [**Disk access rights required when CLO is running**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/17074279996697-Disk-access-rights-required-when-CLO-is-running) * [**How to Speed Up CLO**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/23390057463577-How-to-Speed-Up-CLO) * [**How to Prevent CLO File Corruption**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/23206278838681-How-to-Prevent-CLO-File-Corruption) * [**Graphics Card Problems and Troubleshooting**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000296768-Graphics-Card-Problems-and-Troubleshooting)

title: Avatar Properties
content: **Set the properties of the avatar.** ### 1. Click an avatar with Select/Move tool. 2. Click an avatar. →The properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Adjust each properties below as needed. **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Information** | **Name /** **Item NO.** | Enter a name and an item number of the avatar. **Tech Pack** **(CLO-SET)** | Set whether to include avatar in the Tech Pack or not. **Body Styling** | **Style Configurator** | Set the appearance of the avatar. You can manually set the color of hair, skin, underwear, eyebrows, Eye and lips by clicking the Style Configurator button on the right. **Eye Control** ([![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/25701355515545)](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=Kw_eMEWqBpsPJlNX&t=1647) [Watch Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CwB8_ad328M&t=1647s)) | Adjust the position of the avatar's eyes horizontally or vertically. **📝****Note:** This option is only supported for the new avatars available starting with version 7.2. **Surface** | **Skin Offset** | Adjust the distance between the avatar and the garment. Since the avatar and the garment consist of the meshes, a very high value of particle distance and low value of Skin Offset can cause the avatar to protrude out from under the garment. To prevent this, the default Skin Offset value is set to 3mm, which is the proper value for creating a garment. When you fit your garment accurately or create a fitted garment, lower the value of the Skin Offset. **📝****Note:** Leave the default value until you almost finish your garment, since the simulation is being slow when you lower the Skin Offset of the avatar and the Particle Distance of the garment. **Friction** | Increase the friction value to prevent a garment slipped away while draping or animating. **Static** | The friction when a garment is in stationary position. **Kinetic** | The friction when a garment is moving. **Soft Body Simulation** | Apply deformable body simulation to express skin elasticity. This option is available on CLO's default adult avatar, and can only be simulated with garments. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48890535328537)** Enables softbody simulation for custom avatars without skeletons. _* Soft Body Simulation cannot be executed on a Custom Avatar if the mesh contains**holes** or **self-intersections**._ **📝****Note:** Soft body simulation is reflected when recording animation to enable realistic expression, and soft body simulation can also be applied to 3D dummy or scan files converted to CLO avatars. ([![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/25701355515545)](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=gH3afGW0Szdn4nrZ&t=1881) [Watch Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WRkb4MR0dP0&t=1881s)) **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48890535328537)** ![20252.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51882814533785) NVIDIA GPU is supported starting from version 2025.2. **Divide Mesh** | Adjust the number of the avatar's meshes to smooth the surface of the avatar. Be aware to use this feature when it is necessary. The higher you set the meshes, the bigger the size of the file can cause the slower speed of the program. E.g. This works best when you drape a fitted garment such as leggings since the meshes of the avatar appear. **Material** | Set the [Material](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360047317454-Set-Fabric-Textures) of the avatar.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for adjusting the properties of an avatar, including information on body styling, eye control, surface settings, and material options to enhance your design experience.

title: Sewing Tension
content: **Sewing Tension** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KXPNHZjz29M \- Adjust sewing Tension to improve 3D Garments’ fit. \- Select the ![Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003396367/Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png)**Edit Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Select the Sewing Line which the sewing Tension needs to be adjusted. \- Selected Sewing Line’s properties appear in the Property Editor. * Strength : Type in a value to adjust selected Sewing Line’s Tension Strength. * Ratio : Adjust the Tension Ratio to express how various types of Sewing method influence garment drapes. **※****Note: ** The maximum Tension Ratio is 200%.
content_description: This webpage provides a concise guide on adjusting sewing tension to optimize the fit of 3D garments, featuring a step-by-step tutorial and video resource.

title: Edit 3D Garment
content: **List of Contents** Edit Style Line Scale/ Move Style Line Draw Style Line **Objective** Edit 3D garment easily by moving point and line by keeping its shape. **** **Location** 3D Toolbar **▶![Scale StyleLine.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53431208484249) Edit StyleLine **Tool 3D Toolbar **▶![Scale StyleLine.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53431208484249) Scale StyleLine **Tool 3D Toolbar **▶![Add StyleLine.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53431224771481) Add StyleLine **Tool ## **Operation** **Edit Style Line** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click on the 3D garment to be edited. → Pattern outline and point appear with a black outline. 3. Click on the point ▶ drag and move. → The line and the point sewn are moved together. 4. Or click on the segment ▶ drag it. → The curvature of the line is now adjustable. **Scale/ Move Style Line** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click on the 3D garment to be edited. → Pattern outline and point appear translucent. 3. Click on the segment ▶ drag it. → The garment is scaled or moved with the sewn lines in the drag direction. **Draw Style Line** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click on the 3D garment to be edited. → Pattern outline and point appear translucent. 3. Hover on a Segment, a blue point will appear, click to start the new Style Line. → A point is added to the selected point. 4. Draw a curved line by clicking within the pattern piece, then double click on the segment where you want the new Style Line to end, or draw a straight line by double-clicking the endpoint. → The pattern piece cut along the style line added. **※ Note:** \- The function that allows you to scale or move one side of the sewn lines is excluded in the 6.2 version. The new feature with the improvement of usability will be provided. \- While Editing/Scaling/Moving Style Line, right click to enter the desired dimension. (ver 7.1)
content_description: This web page aims to provide a concise guide for editing, scaling, and drawing style lines on 3D garments using the 3D Toolbar in order to enhance garment design flexibility and precision.
